ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 17758, as amended (the FIU Act), together with its Enforcement Decree and the Financial Transaction Reports Act; the Commercial Act of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended) applicable to Yuhan Hoesa; the Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act; and the Financial Action Task Force Recommendations. Beneficial ownership is captured through financial institution customer due diligence under the FIU Act and reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); there is no public UBO registry for private companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce, Seoul District Court (Supreme Court of Korea registration system)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: official certified copy issued by the Korean court registry; if required abroad, an apostille certificate is attached by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea. No consular legalization is required because Korea is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular legalization is strictly not chained or applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce, Seoul District Court (via Court Registration Information Portal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: court-issued certified English/Korean certificate; if destined for an Apostille Convention country, apostilled by MOFA Korea. No consular legalization is to be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (PoA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa board of directors / shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: signed by directors, notarized by a Korean notary public, then apostilled by MOFA Korea. Consular legalization is not applicable; the apostille is sufficient.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Articles of Incorporation) - certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce, Seoul District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified copy obtained from the court registry, apostilled by MOFA Korea. No consular legalization; do not sequentially add any non-Hague authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Woori Bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank officer signs before a Korean notary public; the notarized letter is then apostilled by MOFA Korea. If issued by a foreign bank for submission to Korea, the foreign bank's signature is notarized and apostilled by the foreign competent authority; no Korean consular legalization is required.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, each shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, and franchise principal must be screened against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit guidance, OFAC SDN and block list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Korean Ministry of Strategy and Finance sanctions measures, and Korean Financial Supervisory Service watchlists. The screening must cover PEPs (foreign and domestic), including their family members and close associates, using a risk-based approach. Negative news, politically exposed person indicators, and adverse media must be reviewed for at least the preceding five years. The bank and the corporate service provider must document the source of funds for the initial contributed capital and any franchise license fees. Enhanced due diligence must be triggered where the beneficial owner is a non-resident or uses a nominee arrangement. A written compliance memorandum with a risk rating and a clearance decision must be approved by the designated compliance officer before opening any bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS (Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea) and the Company Registration Information System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be in Korean script (Hangeul). The name of a Yuhan Hoesa must include a word indicating limited liability, typically the suffix Yuhan Hoesa at the end. English names may be used in the articles of association for international commercial purposes, but the registered name is the Korean script. Foreign names are transliterated phonetically into Hangeul using the official Korean romanization rules; trademark and business identifier conflicts are checked in the registry. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) unique trade name against existing registered companies in the same registry; (2) the corporate form tag Yuhan Hoesa; (3) compatibility with external Franchise Association registrations; and (4) translation consistency for cross-border licensing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Contentious religious or political names without ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the court registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the registry within 14 days from the day after receipt of the rejection notice. The objection must state the grounds and any evidence that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the relevant district court under the Non-Contentious Civil Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal should request a judicial review of the registrar's decision. A licensed Korean attorney must sign the petition. During the appeal the name reservation window remains frozen if a reservation had been granted; otherwise the applicant should reserve at least three alternative names to avoid restarts. This administrative appeal route is the statutory remedy and must be completed before any action before the Constitutional Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in tea-beverage franchise licensing and syrup supply chain, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is legally possible for registration before the court registry, but the National Tax Service (NTS) and commercial banks generally reject a virtual office for this industry because the company must carry physical inventory, maintain a supply warehouse, and handle food-contact materials. The NTS requires a residential or commercial address that appears on the VAT invoice and on the corporate tax return. Where the registered office is a one-room officetel with no business sign, banks impose enhanced due diligence and may refuse to open a corporate account. Thus the operating entity must enter into a physical lease for an office or warehouse in the jurisdiction before the final incorporation filing, and it must display a nameplate corresponding to the registered name.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) presence of a visible company signboard matching the registered name; (2) employees and business records at the address; (3) fire-safety and hygiene permits for the supply warehouse; (4) copy of lease agreement and utility bill; (5) franchise contracts and syrup purchase invoices available. Quantified risk: approximately 35% within the first 24 months for a franchise licensing business due to National Tax Service selective VAT screening and municipal food-safety inspections under the Food Sanitation Act; the risk rises to 55% if the company is a mandatory VAT registrant with turnover close to the minimum taxable threshold. Unannounced visits focus on verifying that the office is not a mere postal address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as last amended; specifically Chapter 6 on the Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under Articles 287-2 to 287-27, Article 289 on Articles of Incorporation, Article 317 on Registration of Incorporation, and Article 318 on the Declaratory Effect of Registration; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 5 and 6 for foreign-invested companies; and the Civil Appeals and Administrative Procedures Act for remedy procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, such as the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, and the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office through the official e-filing portal at iros.go.kr; post-registration tax registration is handled by the District Tax Office of the National Tax Service through HomeTax at hometax.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration and the resulting Certificate of Registered Matters, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the bank certificate of paid-in capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None; the Korean Commercial Act imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa LLC. All subscribed capital must, however, be fully contributed to a Korean bank account in the name of the proposed company before the incorporation registration is filed, and the bank must issue a certificate of paid-in capital. There is no statutory blocked escrow account requirement. For foreign-invested LLCs, the inbound remittance must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; that report is procedural and does not create an escrow condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS OF [COMPANY NAME] YUHAN HOESA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The undersigned members and duly elected managerial directors of [COMPANY NAME] Yuhan Hoesa LLC, acting of their free will and pursuant to Articles 287-3 through 287-13, Article 289, and Article 317(1) of the Korean Commercial Act, adopt the following resolutions by unanimous written consent and waive any requirement for a formal in-person meeting. 1. INCORPORATION AND SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the incorporation of the Company be and is hereby ratified and confirmed in its entirety; that the Company shall operate as a limited liability company formed for the licensed franchise of bubble tea store operations, the manufacture and supply of associated syrups and concentrates, and the collection of franchise royalties; and that the full issued capital of KRW [amount], divided into [number] contribution units, be and is hereby subscribed by the members in the proportions shown in Schedule A. RESOLVED FURTHER that each member shall contribute the subscribed amount in cash to the company pre-incorporation bank account at [bank] at or before the date of registration, and that the bank certificate of paid-in capital be delivered to the registration office. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that [bank] and its designated branch be and is hereby approved as the Company principal depository, settlement, and point-of-sale float banker. The Managing Member and any one co-signatory designated by the Managing Member are hereby authorized to open corporate demand, savings, foreign currency, franchise royalty, and settlement accounts; to sign checks, wire transfer orders, and debit advices; to enroll in and administer home-banking and electronic fund transfers; and to perform all ancillary acts necessary to receive franchise royalties and pay operating expenses. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the Company registered office be and is hereby established at [address], Republic of Korea, with immediate effect. The Managing Member is authorized to execute or amend the office lease, file the registered office with the court registration office, and notify the National Tax Service of any future relocation. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [name] be and is hereby appointed Managing Member and Chief Executive Officer; [name] be appointed General Manager and Corporate Officer; and [name] be appointed Auditor to the extent required by the Commercial Act. Such officers are authorized, jointly or singly, to represent the Company before the court, the National Tax Service, the Fair Trade Commission, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, the Ministry of Environment, and the National Fire Agency; to execute all applications, disclosure statements, and permits; and to establish the operational signature matrix in the corporate seal ledger. All acts performed by them in furtherance of formation, registration, licensing, and bank account opening from the date of incorporation are hereby ratified and confirmed. This Resolution shall be signed by the Managing Member, the General Manager, and the Auditor in the corporate seal book. The members hereby waive any requirement for notice, meeting, or vote under the Commercial Act to the maximum extent permitted for a limited liability company. All officers are instructed to cause this Resolution to be filed in the Company minute book, to deliver certified copies to the registering court, the National Tax Service, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, the Fair Trade Commission, the Ministry of Environment, and the relevant local government, and to pay all necessary registration taxes and user fees. This Resolution shall take effect immediately upon execution, and any prior understanding inconsistent with this Resolution is deemed amended and superseded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, notarization of articles, and capital subscription through bank certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office and the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office at iros.go.kr; any Korean commercial bank; a Korean notary public or licensed law office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation and incorporated-name availability search through the official court e-filing portal; prepare, sign, and notarize the Articles of Incorporation; open a pre-registration capital deposit account in the name of the proposed company at the selected bank and transfer the full subscribed capital; obtain the bank certificate of capital contribution; ensure the stated corporate purpose includes ISIC 5610 franchise licensing and syrup manufacture and supply, and confirm that the appointed officers and signature restrictions are consistent with the corporate governance matrix.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Written consent of the organizers and members
Bank certificate of paid-in capital or capital contribution receipt
Corporate name reservation confirmation
Identification documents and corporate seal registration application
Consent of each proposed statutory officer
Registered office lease agreement or letter of permission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected for identity or similarity with an existing registered name, file three substitute names through the same portal; if notarization is delayed, use a licensed Korean attorney or an official e-notary service to expedite certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court incorporation registration of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office, Registry Division; Supreme Court e-Filing System at www.scourt.go.kr or iros.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the formal application for incorporation registration and submit it to the court registry together with the notarized Articles, the bank capital certificate, the first written resolution, the members consent forms, the registered office proof, the corporate seal certificate, and the application for registration tax payment. Pay the court registration tax and certificate fee at the designated government receipt counter or through the electronic payment system. Upon satisfactory substantive review of the corporate name, purpose, capital, officers, and address, the court will enter the company into the commercial register and issue the Certificate of Registered Matters.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
First board and members written resolution
Consent to appointment of Managing Member, General Manager, and Auditor
Corporate seal certificate and seal impression
Proof of registered office such as lease agreement
Application for incorporation registration
Registration tax payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary document request or correction order, submit the missing instruments through the e-filing system within 14 days; if registration is suspended for a substantive defect, file an application for correction or seek an administrative court remedy under the Administrative Litigation Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the National Tax Service for corporate tax, VAT, and withholding accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Tax Office; online portal HomeTax at hometax.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into HomeTax or visit the District Tax Office within 21 calendar days of court registration and submit the corporate business registration application. Select the primary tax classification as beverage service and franchise operations and the secondary classification as food manufacturing and syrup processing. Designate the registered office address and the physical production site in the same application, register the corporate seal, appoint the Managing Member as the tax representative, and request issuance of a tax invoice certificate. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate and the corporate taxpayer number that must be used for franchise royalty invoices, payroll withholding, and VAT returns.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters from the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate business registration application form
Corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement or free-use consent for the registered office and production site
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Identification documents of the tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a notification rejecting or correcting the business type code, resubmit through HomeTax with a revised ISIC 5610 and NAICS 722515 classification and attach the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety license application receipt; any minor administrative fine can be paid online and corrected through a written objection to the District Tax Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Franchisor registration and disclosure under the Fair Franchise Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Fair Trade Commission, Franchise Transaction Information System at franchise.ftc.go.kr; local Fair Trade Commission regional office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before soliciting any franchisee or receiving any franchise fee, prepare the franchise disclosure statement, standard franchise agreement, financial statements, royalty schedule, syrup supply-chain terms, and all statutory disclosure items prescribed by the Enforcement Decree of the Fair Franchise Transactions Act. File the franchise business registration through the Commission integrated franchise system, paying the applicable registration fee, and obtain the franchise registration number. Once registered, the franchisor must keep the disclosure statement current, deliver a copy to each prospective franchisee at least 14 days before the contract is signed, and publicize the registration number in all franchise advertisements.
required_dossiers: Franchise disclosure statement
Standard franchise agreement containing territorial, royalty, supply, and termination clauses
Financial statements and audit report
Evidence of trademark or trade name rights in the boba tea brand
Business Registration Certificate of the LLC
Food manufacturing license or application pending certificate
Certificate of corporate seal and authority documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commission flags missing annexes or incomplete disclosure, amend and resubmit the package within the prescribed cure period; if the certificate is delayed, submit an expedited amendment application and request a written confirmation of the registration date; continued non-registration is subject to corrective orders and penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food manufacturing, food service, fire safety, civil defense, and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the local district Gu or Gun health and environment office; National Fire Agency and local fire station; Ministry of Employment and Labor regional office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the business registration certificate, floor plans, equipment list, ventilation and wastewater drawings, potable water test, and HACCP plan to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety or its delegated local government office for inspection and issuance of the Food Manufacturing and Processing Business License and the Food Service Business License. In parallel, request a local fire station inspection of fire alarms, fire extinguishers, exit capacity, and kitchen hood suppression, and obtain a structural load clearance from a licensed engineer for syrup tanks and warehouse shelving. After those clearances are issued, finalize the civil defense disaster and evacuation plan with the district safety office and register the workplace under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Facility floor plan and architectural drawings
Equipment list with capacities and utility connections
HACCP plan for syrup manufacturing and boba tea preparation
Potable water quality test report
Wastewater discharge facility report or environmental registration certificate
Fire prevention system completion certificates
Structural load inspection report
Occupational safety and health registration form
Hazardous waste transporter contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety issues a supplementary notice, complete all sanitation upgrades and request re-inspection; if the local government fails to act within the service standard, file an administrative appeal under the Civil Appeals Act and notify the national ombudsman; if fire inspection fails, install the missing fire suppression equipment and reapply through the local fire station.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations and customs verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Yuhan Hoesa (LLC): (1) complete Korean incorporation and commercial registration at the local court, obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation and corporate seal registration; (2) within 20 days of business commencement, submit an Application for Business Registration under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act to the jurisdictional district tax office, physically or through HomeTax electronic authentication; (3) NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as the corporate TIN and VAT ID, and the Business Registration Certificate (Saupja Deungnokjeung) becomes the sole tax identification credential; (4) if the shareholder is a foreign non-resident entity, file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with KOTRA or a licensed foreign exchange bank, and enter the foreign shareholder in the corporate share register - this is not a separate tax registration but may require exchange-control reporting. For a foreign non-resident entity operating through a Korean branch or permanent establishment without forming an incorporated Korean subsidiary, the additional path is: (5) register the domestic place of business with NTS using the Foreign Corporation Domestic Place of Business Registration procedure, appoint a resident tax representative, and obtain the same Business Registration Number; this registration automatically establishes corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding registration obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not allow a check-the-box pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa; a corporation with head office or effective management in Korea is automatically a domestic corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch check-the-box election or comparable elective pass-through regime is available for this structure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, administered by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for a corporation. A Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT before business starts and in all cases no later than 20 days after business commencement. An individual business with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million may qualify as a simplified taxable person, but a corporate legal entity is always a general taxable person and cannot rely on that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoicing is mandatory for all corporations under Article 32 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act. A Yuhan Hoesa must issue an Electronic Tax Invoice (e-Tax Invoice) and transmit it to NTS HomeTax no later than the day following the supply. NTS validates the e-Tax Invoice series, matches it to the taxable person's VAT return and to the counterparty's purchase records, and uses this cross-matching as the anti-fraud clearance mechanism. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp or third-party real-time clearance API; the HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system is the statutory fiscal clearance channel.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying international services are zero-rated under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree. For this franchise business, zero-rating applies to: (a) physical exports of bubble tea syrups, ingredients, packaging, and equipment supplied from Korea to foreign franchisees, evidenced by a Korea Customs Service export declaration through UNI-PASS; and (b) franchise licensing and royalty services supplied to foreign franchisees where the service is effectively consumed or used outside Korea, evidenced by the franchise agreement, foreign country trademark or store operations records, and foreign currency remittance. Domestic supplies to Korean franchisees, including local syrup sales and domestic royalty fees, are subject to 10% VAT and are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Receipt lodged in and approved by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS for physical export of goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international consignment note evidencing movement of goods from Korea to the foreign franchisee destination
Commercial Invoice and Packing List matching the export declaration value, quantity, and consignee

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency from the foreign franchisee

For franchise service zero-rating: executed franchise agreement, evidence of offshore use or consumption of the licensed rights, service completion records, and corresponding inbound foreign-currency payment records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export zero-rating by matching UNI-PASS export declarations, foreign exchange remittance confirmations from Korean banks, and e-Tax Invoice records. If the required customs, logistics, or FX repatriation documentation is missing, incomplete, or inconsistent, NTS will reclassify the export as a taxable domestic supply, assess 10% VAT on the full unreported value, disallow related input VAT credits, and reassess corporate income tax accordingly. Statutory additional taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes apply, and serious or fictitious export claims are referred to the public prosecutor under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, the Customs Act, and the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes. Retrospective reassessment and clawback are permitted under the National Tax Basic Act limitation periods: 5 years for ordinary omissions and 10 years for fraudulent or deceptive omissions, with interest and penalties accruing from the original return due date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) with regulatory execution by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalized but supervised convertibility regime. Current-account transactions for franchise royalties, management fees, and goods import/export settlement are generally free from prior approval, yet they require the underlying transaction to be reported through authorized domestic banks using standardized foreign exchange declaration forms. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity injection and foreign-direct-investment (FDI) funded working capital, are not freely convertible without registration; the foreign investor must file an FDI declaration with KOTRA or a registered receiving bank, open a foreign-currency account, and document the exact business purpose before converting to Korean won. There is no mandatory forex surrender quota for exporters, but all inward remittance must pass through a licensed foreign exchange bank, and the bank is obliged to verify the remittance route, purpose code, and tax status. Profit remittance is permitted after corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax settlement, provided the entity produces audited financial statements, an external audit report where required, a certificate of tax clearance, and a valid foreign-exchange transaction report. The practical bottleneck is not legal prohibition but documentation density; the Bank of Korea and KoFIU expect an A-Z evidentiary trail covering UBOs, source of funds, business substance, and tax compliance before each large outward payout is cleared.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected by the Korean exporting entity within 6 months from the date of the export declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; extensions can be granted by the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the receiving bank for a documented period if the exporter demonstrates justifiable delay such as non-payment by the overseas franchise. There is no mandatory publicly fixed percentage of export receipts that must be surrendered into Korean won; exporters may retain collections in their corporate foreign-currency account or convert to KRW at a licensed bank's market rate. However, the bank must be given a copy of the export customs declaration, the commercial invoice, the bill of lading, and the foreign exchange transaction report showing the expected payment date; any collection beyond the six-month window triggers an overdue export-report filing and may expose the entity to administrative penalties or AML escalation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Current Account
FDI Capital Depot Account and Trade Services Current Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account with Won Conversion and Clearing Account
Corporate Current Account and LC/Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as global neo-banking treasury tools do not qualify as deposit-taking institutions under the Korean Banking Act; they cannot issue a corporate KRW account, cannot link to the Korean tax administration's electronic cash-receipt system, and cannot process the statutory Foreign Exchange Transactions Report on behalf of a Korean resident entity. Fintech EMIs may be used only as an auxiliary payment collector for non-Korean franchisees if those merchants prefer card/MCAD payments, but the primary operating treasury, FDI escrowing, and trade settlement must remain with a commercial bank licensed by the FSC. Using a foreign EMI as the main treasury rail would create a significant KYC gap because the Korean depository bank cannot verify the source of KRW funding and KoFIU would flag the structure as an unlicensed money-service operation. Therefore, treasury architects should not propose any cross-border EMI as the settlement spine for the Yuhan Hoesa franchise; a licensed domestic bank is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa whose ultimate overseas beneficiary is the shareholder, the statutory representative or a director with actual operational authority must appear physically at a domestic branch for the initial Corporate Securities/KYC interview under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FSC AML regulations. Remote consular proxy opening is not a universally recognized route: if no director can fly to Korea, banks usually accept a consularized/notarized power of attorney in favor of a Korean-licensed certified public accountant or a resident officer, but that person must still attend an in-branch interview and be video-recorded with the non-resident UBO participating by secure conference. The bank will require apostilled articles of incorporation, a board resolution designating the account signatories, a notarized UBO declaration, and evidence of the real business location (lease contract of franchise headquarters or licensed kitchen/syrup warehouse) before activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified beneficial ownership chain through the overseas franchise aggregator and brand licensor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and memorandum of association for every shareholder above 10%; current shareholder registry; trust structure flowcharts if any; passport pages of natural-person UBOs; foreign government-issued proof of address; embassy consular legalization; original or certified copy of the FTCDMS/FDIS foreign investment registration card issued by KOTRA or the receiving bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion that initial equity capital is actually a disguised loan or uncommitted commercial funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month domestic and overseas bank statements of remitting entities; signed share subscription agreement; board resolution valuing minority rights; audited financial statements of the parent or beneficial owner; source-of-wealth documents including asset liquidation agreements, gift deeds, inheritance records, employment income, or monetized receivable contracts; tax returns and tax residence certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, adverse-media, or sanctions screening have edge matches due to Korean/Chinese romanization differences
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal identity verification letters from financial institutions where the shareholder banks; name-alias certificate from the passport-issuing authority; a negative-media search package from a registered compliance data vendor; a reaffirmed PEP declaration signed by UBOs; any court/political-reputation background records with brief considered statements; certified translations of all public record pages.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and syrup-transaction flows do not resemble a brick-and-mortar franchise and may be construed as phantom trade between related parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master franchise and area development agreements; detailed royalty calculation schedules; cloud dashboard showing monthly store sales and quality inspections; warehouse storage and logistics service contracts; Korean beverage research/development or production license, HACCP certificate, customs export declarations and K-Unipass shipping records; VAT invoices and corporate tax returns for the previous 12 months; minutes of board meetings approving each cross-border payout.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity must be preceded by a Foreign Investment (FDI) declaration through KOTRA or the receiving tier-1 bank in Korea. The remitting overseas franchise operator should wire USD or KRW using SWIFT MT103 and clearly reference the FIPA declaration number, the target company name, and the capital purpose in field 70; a reference to personal expense, salary, or unspecified loan will be rejected by the Korean clearing bank. The receiving bank then validates the foreign exchange purpose code, screens the counterparty, and transfers the funds into a temporarily held Foreign Currency Deposit Account before converting to KRW at the market rate. Within one month, the Yuhan Hoesa must retain an external certified accountant to produce a paid-in capital verification report and secure the Foreign Investor Registration Certificate. This certificate must be delivered to the depository bank, the ADB, and the tax office before the working capital can be treated as free corporate funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For franchise royalty and management service payments to the overseas brand owner, the clearing rail should be a SWIFT MT103 wire backed by the signed franchise contract, a Korean tax invoice with VAT, and evidence of withholding tax payment to the National Tax Service. For physical syrup, tapioca pearls, packaging, and equipment, the rail should be a commercial letter of credit under SWIFT MT700 or a documentary collection route, with required documents being commercial invoice, packing list, insurance certificate, bill of lading or cargo receipt, K-Unipass export declaration, and the applicable health/food import certificate. Domestic franchise stores collecting from consumers in Korea use local POS rails cleared through Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC) with KRW settlement; no international SWIFT charge is required. All outbound disbursements are subject to bank verification that the operation has a valid Foreign Exchange Transaction Report and that the beneficiary exists in the real economy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts for documented franchise royalty receivables and confirmed syrup import payables; tenors normally up to 12 months and cannot be speculative

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts with an authorized Korean bank or an offshore bank acting through a Korean branch, only where the underlying operating cash flow is contractual and verifiable through invoices and tax returns

Cross-currency interest rate and currency swaps between KRW and USD with licensed dealing banks, used to hedge long-term franchise capex or foreign-currency bank loans where the notional amortization schedule matches actual repayment dates

Exchange-traded KRW/USD futures on KRX or OTC plain-vanilla currency options with strikes tied to budgeted franchise margin; exotic structured products with knockout or auto-call features are prohibited for this low-risk treasury profile

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and local corporate income tax surcharge return, including annual financial statements and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; local government tax authorities (Si/Gun/Gu) for the local income tax surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: by 31 March of the following year. Non-calendar fiscal year: within 3 months after the fiscal year-end. For entities subject to external audit, the NTS e-filing extension may extend the filing to 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return: 20% of unpaid corporate tax as negligence penalty; underreported tax: 10% negligence penalty; unpaid tax accrues late-payment interest at 0.022% per day from the original due date; prolonged delinquency may trigger tax seizure, business suspension, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Administrative strike-off is not automatic for tax delinquency, but a dormant company continuously failing to operate and file can be judicially dissolved by the court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the franchise information disclosure document under the Fair Franchise Transactions Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC), Franchise Transaction Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year and in any event before the one-year anniversary of the current registration; a material-change amendment must be filed within 30 days of the relevant change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A void renewal prevents Yuhan Hoesa from entering into any new franchise agreements; KFTC may issue corrective orders and impose an administrative fine not exceeding KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 75,000); serious violations may also be publicly disclosed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report filing by an independent certified CPA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART; copy attached to the NTS corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa subject to audit: the report must be completed and filed with the FSS no later than 30 April; in all cases before the ordinary members' meeting, which must be held by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or submit the audit report may result in FSS designation of an auditor, administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (up to KRW 50,000,000, approximately USD 37,500), and civil liability of directors and the auditor for damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary members' meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No regulator receives the minutes; they must be retained at the registered office and made available to members and the court upon request. If the meeting approves any director, member, or capitalization change subject to registration, the competent Court Registry must be notified.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of each fiscal year; calendar-year entity: no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting does not create a tax penalty, but resolutions and financial statement approvals may be invalid if the procedure is defective; directors may be subject to civil liability and the company may be exposed to court petitions for deadlock resolution. Failure to maintain or falsify the minute book is a criminal/administrative offence under the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry change filing and beneficial-ownership event reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent District Court Registry Office (Commercial Registration Section); Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or designated foreign-exchange bank for foreign investment acquisition reports
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the underlying event for court registration; foreign investors acquiring Yuhan Hoesa equity must file a foreign investment report within 30 days after the acquisition. If no event occurs, no annual registry filing is required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registry filing subjects the company to negligence penalties under the Commercial Act and may invalidate the legal effect against good-faith third parties; failure to report a foreign investment may trigger penalty provisions and fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit applies to a Yuhan Hoesa if, as of the fiscal year-end, it meets any one of: total assets at least KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); total revenue at least KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500,000); average full-time employees at least 300; or it is otherwise designated under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including being a financial institution or a listed company. A voluntary audit may also be required if members holding at least 10% of the equity request it or if the company applies for preferential tax status requiring certified financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for audit-required entities; Korean GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards) or SME Accounting Standards for eligible non-listed small and medium-sized entities; statutory books and tax reconciliations must also comply with the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not currently require a private Yuhan Hoesa to file a separate annual UBO confirmation return with the commercial registry. Beneficial-ownership and shareholding accuracy is enforced through event-driven filings: every transfer of member equity must be recorded in the Register of Members, and where the transferee is a foreign investor acquiring 10% or more of the equity, a foreign investment report must be submitted to KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of the transfer closing; any resulting change in directors, members, or registered capital must be filed with the competent Court Registry within 2 weeks. As part of annual corporate secretarial maintenance, the company must confirm that the Register of Members, internal UBO/KYC records, and the Registered Agent file are consistent and are retained for at least 7 years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per year for a registered office/corporate secretarial agent in Seoul or another metropolitan jurisdiction, including annual compliance calendar management and standard court-registry filings.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 25,000 for a statutory CPA audit for a small/mid-sized Yuhan Hoesa franchise licensee/supply-chain company; USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 for a non-statutory review or compilation if audit thresholds are not met.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (applicable to taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; lower progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion; plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax, yielding a combined top effective rate of 27.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and reductions available under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act (STTCA) for foreign-invested businesses in free economic zones (FEZ) or foreign investment zones (100% exemption for 5 years, 50% for the following 2 years for qualifying high-tech businesses); R&D tax credits up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D expenditures; no patent box regime, but transfer of qualifying intellectual property may be eligible for capital gains treatment or withholding tax exemptions under domestic law or tax treaties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Domestic Corporations (Form No. 21, attached schedules) filed via HomeTax (hometax.go.kr), the National Tax Service (NTS) electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (each fiscal year; with quarterly or semi-annual advance corporate tax payments for companies with prior-year taxable income exceeding a statutory threshold; final return due within 3 months of fiscal year-end)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate income tax return must be filed by the end of the third month following the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end: filing deadline March 31). An extension of up to one month is available for groups with foreign subsidiaries or foreign accounting standards (under Art. 60(4) of the Corporate Income Tax Act), filed via the NTS with a revised statutory due date (April 30).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification details: business registration number, legal entity name, domestic representative, registered address, fiscal year, business purpose (ISIC 5610 – food and beverage service activities; franchise royalty and supply chain).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the foreign shareholder's name and nationality in the attached shareholders' schedule. For non-resident owners, the Korean company must withhold income tax on outbound payments under the Corporate Tax Act and the ITA. Ensure the company's domestic tax representative is registered with the NTS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Financial Statements / Income Statement Line Items)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of sales, selling, general and administrative expenses, operating income, non-operating income/expenses, and net income before tax per Korean GAAP (K-IFRS or general corporate accounting standards).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all worldwide income for Korean domestic corporations (unlimited tax liability). For revenue from global franchise royalties, recognize the income on an accrual basis; for intercompany transactions with overseas affiliates, apply the arm's length principle and prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation to support the revenue and expense allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 (Taxable Income Adjustments – Additions and Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of adjustments to book net income to arrive at taxable income: nondeductible expenses, non-taxable income, depreciation adjustments, reserve/reversal adjustments, and foreign tax credit carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any intercompany royalties or management fees that fail the arm's length standard and are not substantiated by a written agreement. Deduct only expenses directly related to Korean-source income and supported by proper tax invoices (e-tax invoices) or receipts. For cross-border royalty expense payments, verify that the withholding tax was properly applied and the treaty beneficial ownership form is on file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit (FTC), R&D tax credit, employment-related tax credits, and territorial/international double-tax relief calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an inbound franchise or supply chain, if the Korean company has paid foreign withholding taxes on outbound royalties or interest, the foreign tax credit may be claimed only if the income is included in Korean taxable income and the foreign tax is legally imposed. Attach the FTC schedule and preserve the foreign tax receipt documentation. For the Korean entity receiving income from overseas franchisees, the FTC is available for foreign taxes paid on Korean-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax (surtax) equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax payable, reported on the separate local tax return form but integrated in the filing package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local income tax is not creditable against foreign taxes. Ensure that the local surtax due is separately remitted to the local government through the HomeTax system. Failure to remit may trigger separate interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of payments made to non-residents, including dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees, and the withheld Korean income tax at statutory or treaty-reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each outbound payment to a non-resident shareholder, lender, franchise licensor, or supplier, the Korean company is legally required to withhold at source. If a tax treaty reduces the rate, obtain the non-resident's Tax Residence Certificate (TRC), beneficial ownership statement (Form 24-1 for dividends, or applicable NTS form), and any additional documentary evidence (e.g., certificate of residence issued within the past 12 months). For royalties related to trademarks, know-how, or franchise formulas, the DTA rate is 10-15%, but only if the non-resident is the beneficial owner and has no permanent establishment in Korea. Interest may be subject to 20-22% direct rate, or treaty-reduced to 10-15%. Do not remit the gross amount until the withholding tax has been remitted to the NTS and the non-resident received a withholding receipt (Form No. 24).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of the unpaid tax if the gross revenue exceeds KRW 1 billion (otherwise 10%); if the return is filed after the statutory deadline, additional daily surcharges of 0.022% per day (capped at 0.75% per month / no cap after 1 month) apply; non-payment of withheld taxes by the 10th of the following month triggers 20% penalty plus 0.025% daily surcharge; intentional or fraudulent underreporting of tax basis may constitute tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years (or up to 10 years for evasion exceeding KRW 500 million) and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax + 2% local income tax surtax) on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a treaty-reduced rate (e.g., 10% or 15% under most OECD DTAs), the Korean company must, prior to remittance, obtain from the non-resident payee: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the jurisdiction of residence, dated within 12 months of the payment; (2) a completed Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaty (Form No. 24 or 24-1, as applicable); (3) a Beneficial Ownership Statement confirming the payee is the true owner, receives the income for its own benefit, and does not merely act as an intermediary; (4) evidence that the non-resident does not have a permanent establishment in Korea to which the income is effectively connected. The NTS may review the economic substance through anti-abuse rules (IFA) and treaty shopping provisions. If the application is approved, the reduced rate is applied in the withholding filing; otherwise, the full 22% must be withheld and the refund of any over-withholding must be pursued through a supplementary tax return or refund process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 22% (20% national + 2% local) unless treaty-reduced (usually 10% or 15% for franchise/industrial/commercial/scientific royalties; interest: statutory rate 22% unless treaty-reduced (typically 10% or 15% for interest payable to a financial institution or associated enterprise). For interest paid to a foreign bank without a Korean PE, a 25.6% rate may apply before treaty relief. Documentation required: TRC, beneficial ownership certificate, and a debt restructure or royalty agreement demonstrating arm's length substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (total intercompany transactions with foreign related parties in the fiscal year) for Master File and Local File preparation; KRW 5 billion for local file only; lower thresholds apply for cross-border intercompany service transactions (KRW 1 billion) and indirect contracts (KRW 5 billion). Contemporaneous documentation must be prepared by the tax return due date and submitted within 60 days of an NTS request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Korea Tax Treaty Act, the NTS applies a substance-over-form doctrine. For a Yuhan Hoesa acting as a franchise master or supply chain hub, it must demonstrate that its core income-generating activities (CIGA) – e.g., contract negotiation, logistics coordination, quality control, regional marketing, and IP management – are economically occurred in Korea. If the entity is merely a shell that receives royalty or resale income without substantive employees, premises, or functions, the NTS may disregard the entity's legal form, reallocate income to the beneficial owner, and deny treaty benefits under the Limitation on Benefits (LOB) or principal purpose test (PPT).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting franchise royalty income, inflating deductible intercompany management fees or supply costs to shift profit abroad, or submitting false financial statements to the NTS; also failing to withhold and remit non-resident tax on outbound royalties/dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, intentional tax evasion (underreporting taxable income or claiming fraudulent deductions) is punishable with imprisonment for up to 5 years or fines up to 3 times the evaded tax; if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million, imprisonment of up to 10 years; additional 40% of the evaded tax as an administrative surcharge under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the concealment or who approve false filings are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties (corporate veil pierced); criminal conviction leads to imprisonment; the NTS may blacklist the director, impose travel bans, and attach personal assets for restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting cross-border intercompany transactions with related parties (e.g., global franchise parent, syrup supplier, IP holding company) at non-arm's length prices, or failing to prepare and submit contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local/Master File) within the statutory deadline, thus enabling the NTS to adjust taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 6 of the Act on Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the NTS may re-determine the arm's length price and assess additional corporate income tax, plus an underreporting penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted profit; if documents are not provided, a penalty of up to KRW 100 million may apply per document (Article 11(3)).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the transfer pricing controls or knowingly cause the non-arm's length documentation to be suppressed are liable for the resulting tax delinquency; the NTS can seek civil damages from the directors for failure to exercise due diligence; in egregious cases, the director's personal assets (bank accounts, properties) can be frozen and attached.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Beneficial Ownership Abuse (Anti-Money Laundering & Treaty Shopping)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Yuhan Hoesa as a shell entity with no real business premises, employees, or economic functions in Korea, or routing deductible royalties/dividends through a tax-haven intermediary purely to obtain treaty benefits or to obscure the ultimate shareholder; failing to declare the ultimate beneficial owner in AML/KYC filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Treaty Act (Article 30-2) and the Financial Transaction Reports Act, treaty shopping and sham transactions are denied treaty benefits; the NTS imposes ordinary corporate tax at 22% (27.5% effective) plus a 20% penalty for unjustified tax benefits; the Financial Services Commission may impose administrative fines up to KRW 50 million; repeated violations may lead to business registration cancellation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly form or maintain a sham entity are personally liable for the disgorgement of all tax benefits; they may face criminal charges for fraud or breach of fiduciary duty under the Commercial Act, leading to imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to KRW 100 million; directors may also be subject to an international travel ban and Interpol red notice if assets are secreted abroad.
